title_en: Midas’ Winmill on Free Cash Flow Over Narratives
title_zh: Midas 的 Tom Windmill 谈自由现金流高于叙事
subtitle_zh: Tom Windmill 谈以每股自由现金流和资本回报率为核心、弱化叙事的选股之道
description: Midas’ Winmill on Free Cash Flow Over Narratives

turns.en: Welcome to Inside Active, a podcast about active managers who goes beyond soundbites and headlines and looks deeper into their processes, challenges, and philosophies in security selection.
turns.zh: 欢迎收听 Inside Active，这是一档关于主动管理型基金经理的播客，我们不满足于金句和标题，而是深入探讨他们在证券选择（security selection）上的流程、挑战和理念。

turns.en: I'm David Cohn.
turns.zh: 我是 David Cohn。

turns.en: I lead mutual fund and active research at Bloomberg Intelligence. One of the promises of active management is flexibility, the ability to go where the opportunities are rather than being constrained by an index, a particular style, or even a specific part of the market. But having a broad opportunity set also presents a challenge. When you can invest across sectors, market caps, and different types of securities, you need a disciplined framework for deciding what deserves a place in the portfolio. So today, I wanted to explore what that type of framework looks like in practice, how an active manager defines quality, generates ideas, determines what a business is worth, and ultimately decides when conviction is strong enough to make a meaningful investment. So joining me to discuss that is Tom Windmill, President and Director of the Midas Family of Mutual Funds and Portfolio Manager of the Midas Special Opportunities Fund, ticker MISEX. Tom, thanks for joining me. Hey, it's a pleasure, David. As always, I love your podcast. You're very important in it. Well, thank you so much and appreciate you joining me. So, Tom, the mandate for Midas Special Opportunities is, I'd say, unusually broad. You can invest across asset classes, market caps, sectors, geographies. When you have that much freedom, what actually defines your investment philosophy?
turns.zh: 我在 Bloomberg Intelligence 负责共同基金和主动管理研究。主动管理的一大承诺就是灵活性——能够去机会所在的地方，而不是被某个指数、某种特定风格、甚至市场的某个特定板块所束缚。但拥有广泛的机会集同时也带来挑战。当你可以跨行业、跨市值、跨不同类型的证券进行投资时，你需要一套有纪律的框架来判断什么才值得在投资组合中占据一席之地。所以今天，我想探讨这种框架在实践中是什么样子——一位主动管理者如何定义质量、如何产生投资想法、如何判断一家企业的价值，以及最终如何决定信念强到什么程度才值得下重注。那么，今天和我一起讨论这个话题的是 Tom Windmill，他是 Midas Family of Mutual Funds 的总裁兼董事，也是 Midas Special Opportunities Fund（代码 MISEX）的基金经理。Tom，谢谢你来做客。嘿，我很荣幸，David。一如既往，我很喜欢你的播客。你在里面很重要。嗯，非常感谢，也很感谢你来参加。那么 Tom，Midas Special Opportunities 的授权范围，我得说，异常宽泛。你可以跨资产类别、市值、行业、地域进行投资。当你有这么大的自由度时，究竟是什么定义了你的投资理念？

turns.en: I would say that our investment philosophy is based on the view that a business is something that you put a dollar into and you get more than a dollar of free cash flow back. And with that basic idea, I guess if I had to shoehorn us into some type of recognized theory of investing, that would be GARP. But it's the garb of growth at a reasonable price. Growth is free cash flow per share. Free cash flow per share is what we are pursuing. And that is what defines our philosophy. So if we can find any kind of investment with growing free cash flow for our share of dollar in, we're very interested. Okay.
turns.zh: 我会说，我们的投资理念基于这样一个观点：一家企业就是你投入一美元、然后能拿回超过一美元自由现金流（free cash flow）的东西。有了这个基本想法，我想如果非要硬把我们塞进某种公认的投资理论里，那就是 GARP。也就是合理价格成长（growth at a reasonable price）的外衣。这里的成长指的是每股自由现金流（free cash flow per share）。每股自由现金流才是我们追求的东西，这也正是定义我们理念的核心。所以，只要能找到任何一种、我们投入的每一美元都能带来不断增长自由现金流的投资，我们都会非常感兴趣。好的。

turns.en: Now, I know another thing you look for is quality companies, but quality can mean very different things to different investors. You know, what are the two or three characteristics that tell you a business is actually high quality?
turns.zh: 那么，我知道你还看重的另一点是优质公司，但对不同的投资者来说，“质量”可能意味着非常不同的东西。你说说看，有哪两三个特征能让你判断一家企业确实是高质量的？

turns.en: Well, as I say, you know, a really good business from a shareholder standpoint has good free cash flow per share. And we like to see that in growth, because with growth, you can have the compounding effect that everyone is seeking. But the other part of what we look for is return on capital employed, not just return on invested capital, which is the business. We want to see how management is deploying all the capital at their disposal. So if you have growing free cash flow per share and a high return on capital employed over, say, a five-year period, you're in very good company. And that's the kind of quality that we look for. Although, you know, it's true that high-quality businesses have characteristics that travel together. So a good earnings yield, free cash flow yield, you know, everything kind of works out, return on assets for a quality business.
turns.zh: 嗯，就像我说的，从股东的角度看，一家真正好的企业拥有良好的每股自由现金流。而且我们喜欢看到它在增长，因为有了增长，你才能得到人人都在追求的复利效应（compounding effect）。但我们看重的另一部分是已动用资本回报率（return on capital employed），而不仅仅是投入资本回报率（return on invested capital）——后者衡量的是企业本身。我们想看的是管理层如何调配他们手中可支配的全部资本。所以，如果一家企业在比如五年时间里，每股自由现金流不断增长，同时已动用资本回报率又很高，那你就进入了非常优秀的公司行列。这正是我们所寻找的那种质量。当然，确实如此，高质量企业的各项特征是相伴而行的。所以，一家优质企业会有不错的盈利收益率（earnings yield）、自由现金流收益率，还有资产回报率（return on assets），一切都能对得上。

turns.en: Okay. So I kind of want to go a little deeper into management because it seems like that's also central to your thesis. You know, in addition to quantitative numbers, you know, like you mentioned the return on capital, you know, what truly separates a management team you're willing to entrust a meaningful amount of capital to from one that, you know, may run a great business, but simply, you know, is not right for the fund? Is there a kind of qualitative aspects?
turns.zh: 好的。那我想更深入地谈谈管理层，因为这似乎也是你投资逻辑的核心。除了你提到的资本回报率这类量化数字之外，究竟是什么真正区分了一个你愿意托付大量资金的管理团队，和一个——虽然可能经营着一家很棒的企业、但就是不适合我们基金的管理团队？这里面有没有一些定性的方面？

turns.en: That's right. You know, it's hard to judge a management team from an interaction. Some of you may have the chemical, a favorable or unfavorable one or whatever. For us, it's really simple. Is this the same management scene that has produced the track record of free cash flow per share growth and return on capital employed that has been the history of the company? So we avoid companies with turnover in the C-suite, if you will, or where they have to hire from someone outside of the company. Those are kind of red flags. But if everything is fine, it's the same management company with a five or 10 year period, you know, great track record of things we're looking for. I don't really need to talk to them. So I assume management is good because of what they've done. Okay.
turns.zh: 没错。你知道，光靠一次接触是很难判断一个管理团队的。有些人你可能会有那种化学反应——有好有坏，或者别的什么。但对我们来说，这其实很简单：这是否还是那支创造出了公司历史上每股自由现金流增长和已动用资本回报率业绩记录的同一批管理层？所以我们会避开高管层（C-suite）出现人事变动的公司，或者那些不得不从公司外部招人的公司。这些都算是危险信号（red flags）。但如果一切都没问题，还是同一批管理层，在五年或十年的时间里有着我们所看重的那些出色业绩记录，那我其实并不需要跟他们谈话。所以我会假定管理层是优秀的，因为他们已经做出的成绩摆在那里。好的。

turns.en: You know, another thing, you know, with a fund like this is it's not constrained by either growth or value. You know, we see that with a lot of funds that are either, you know, very style specific, How do you think about the distinction between growth and value? Does valuation ultimately play a role that can turn a great company into a great investment?
turns.zh: 你知道，像这样的基金还有一点，就是它既不受成长风格的约束，也不受价值风格的约束。我们看到很多基金都是——你知道——非常特定于某种风格的。那你是如何看待成长与价值之间的区别的？估值最终会不会起到那种把一家伟大的公司变成一笔伟大投资的作用？

turns.en: It can. I think the deciding factor, David, is the margin of error. So the better the company, the greater the characteristics that we're looking for, we can accept a higher valuation because we don't need the margin for error. If it's a company we have questions about, maybe it's a new investment for us, before we've really gotten to know it, entry price is more important. So we need a higher margin of error, so we need a lower entry price. So the other characteristic is that a low entry price is more important with a shorter time horizon. So if you have a great company, we think this company is going to be in a dominant market position for 10 years, we can accept a higher entry price. So It's not really a question of growth or value. We kind of look at the entry price as the decider as to whether this is more of a high-risk kind of a value play. We need a low entry price, or this is a company that's going to grow over a 10-year time period, and we can accept a higher valuation price. It'd be more of a growth company.
turns.zh: 会的。我觉得决定性的因素，David，是安全边际（margin of error）。公司越好、我们所看重的特征越突出，我们就越能接受更高的估值，因为我们不需要那么多安全边际。如果是一家我们还有疑问的公司，也许对我们来说是一笔新投资，在我们还没真正了解它之前，买入价格就更重要。所以我们需要更高的安全边际，也就意味着需要更低的买入价。另一个特征是，时间跨度越短，低买入价就越重要。所以如果是一家很棒的公司，我们认为这家公司在未来十年都会占据主导市场地位，那我们就能接受更高的买入价。因此这其实并不是成长还是价值的问题。我们更多是把买入价当作决定因素：这到底是一笔高风险的价值型投资——那我们需要低买入价；还是一家会在十年时间里不断成长的公司——那我们就能接受更高的估值价格，它更偏向一家成长型公司。

turns.en: I understand that obviously a stronger company deserves a higher multiple. What type of valuations do you look at? How do you determine how much you're going to pay?
turns.zh: 我明白，显然更强的公司理应获得更高的估值倍数。那你会看哪些类型的估值？你是如何决定自己要出多少钱的？

turns.en: That is a great question. It's a bit of a cop-out to say this, but we have this famous kind of pigs at the trough view. We have some terrific companies. We think, we hope, we own the best companies in the world. For Another company to get its position at the trough, it has to be better than what we currently own. So we're always looking to upgrade our businesses. So if our fantastic businesses have a certain free cash flow yield, if you will, another one's going to have to have a better free cash flow yield and better prospects for one. So it's a floating number. If we're not leveraged, which we can be, We basically like to see a return on assets, I don't know, maybe better than 15%, but we look for return on capital employed. We'd like to keep the average in the portfolio over 20%, perhaps 25% if we can manage it over a five-year period. Okay.
turns.zh: 这是个好问题。这么说有点像是回避问题，但我们有一套很有名的、类似“猪在食槽边”（pigs at the trough）的观点。我们持有一些极好的公司。我们认为——也希望——我们拥有的是世界上最好的公司。要让另一家公司挤到食槽边占据位置，它必须比我们目前持有的更好。所以我们总是在想办法升级我们的企业组合。因此，如果我们那些极好的公司拥有某个特定的自由现金流收益率，那么另一家公司就必须有更好的自由现金流收益率和更好的前景才行。所以这是一个浮动的数字。如果我们没有使用杠杆——虽然我们是可以用的——我们基本上希望看到资产回报率大概在，我不知道，也许高于 15%，但我们更看重已动用资本回报率。我们希望把投资组合里的平均水平保持在 20% 以上，如果能在五年时间里做到 25% 那就更好了。好的。

turns.en: The other thing I wanted to ask before we kind of get into the process is your definition of risk. I know different managers have different definitions. Investors typically think of standard deviation and volatility, but How do you think about risk? Is it volatility, permanent impairment of capital, paying too much, being wrong about the business?
turns.zh: 在我们进入投资流程之前，我还想问一件事，就是你对风险的定义。我知道不同的经理人有不同的定义。投资者通常会想到标准差和波动率，但你是如何看待风险的？风险是波动率、是资本的永久性损失、是买得太贵、还是对企业的判断出错？

turns.en: How do you think about it? Risk is everywhere, and it's a lovely thing to be able to quantify it, and then you can compare and so on and so forth. And I hate to say it, but I think Warren Buffett said it best. Of course, he said everything best. But he said risk is not knowing what you're doing and not knowing what you own. So we spend a lot of time trying to mitigate risk By knowing what we're doing, so we're always learning from podcasts such as yours, David.
turns.zh: 你怎么看呢？风险无处不在，能够把它量化是件很美妙的事，然后你就可以做比较等等。虽然我不太想这么说，但我觉得 Warren Buffett 说得最好。当然，他说什么都是最好的。他说，风险就是不知道自己在做什么、不知道自己拥有什么。所以我们花了很多时间，通过弄清楚自己在做什么来设法降低风险，因此我们一直在从像你这样的播客里学习，David。

turns.en: Oh, thank you.
turns.zh: 哦，谢谢。

turns.en: And we also spend a lot of time on trying to understand what we own. We read everything we can about it, their own disclosures. Occasionally, I'll read some other commentary. Basically, I'm looking for disconfirming evidence. And we try to focus on the key factors. I remember one time in another portfolio, I was at a mine tour. We were looking at a gold mine in Mexico. And one of the analysts looked at this mine, and this is a huge company, multi-billions, a number of different mines. And she asked the mining engineer, give me a sator. Now, is that pipe one quarter inch or one half inch? And my feeling is, well, that's not actually going to change the risk characteristics or the potential characteristics of this company. So we focus on a bunch of key numbers. We've talked about them already. There are a number of other ones that, as I say, travel together with a quality business. We want to make sure that checks all those boxes. And that is what, how we mitigate risk.
turns.zh: 我们也花很多时间去弄明白自己到底拥有什么。我们会读一切能读到的东西，包括他们自己的披露文件。偶尔我也会读一些其他的评论。基本上，我要找的是反面的证据（disconfirming evidence）。我们会尽量聚焦于关键因素。我记得有一次在另一个投资组合里，我参加了一次矿山参观。我们在看墨西哥的一座金矿。其中一位分析师看着这座矿——而这是一家巨大的公司，市值好几十亿，有好几座不同的矿。她问那位采矿工程师，“给我说说”，那根管子是四分之一英寸还是二分之一英寸？而我的感觉是，嗯，这其实并不会改变这家公司的风险特征或潜力特征。所以我们聚焦于一堆关键的数字。我们已经谈过其中一些了。还有一些其他的数字，就像我说的，会与一家优质企业相伴而行。我们要确保它把这些方框全都勾上。这就是我们降低风险的方式。

turns.en: Okay.
turns.zh: 好的。

turns.en: Got it.
turns.zh: 明白。

turns.en: Uh, fair enough. Um, so if we get into more of the process, how do you generate new investment ideas that, you know, are your opportunities coming from screens, just research company meetings or somewhere else?
turns.zh: 呃，有道理。嗯，那如果我们再深入谈谈流程，你是如何产生新的投资想法的？你知道，你的机会是来自筛选（screens）、公司调研会议，还是别的地方？

turns.en: Yeah. Well, again, to quote, you know, who, you know, Warren WB, I'll What we like to do is kind of hang around the hoop, as I call it. We're not jumping over three-foot hurdles. We like the six-inch hurdle. So I run a screen regularly, and I look for these characteristics. I look for the kind of companies that are super free cash flow generators historically. They've got revenue growth in there, and for some reason, they sell at a low enterprise value to free cash flow multiple. It's like, how did Salesforce get in here? How did all these great companies suddenly drop? into our lap? I'm not a basketball player, but I understand some of the games. I'm not shooting three-pointers. I'm waiting for that easy rebound. Hey, here's a little company just dropped into my hands and there's no one else deflecting it. I can jump up and make a layup. That's what we're looking for. Running screens, looking for our key fundamental indicators. I really never look at street research. I don't look at most commentary. I just stick to our numbers to get started. Okay.
turns.zh: 是啊。嗯，还是引用那位，你知道，Warren Buffett 的话吧。我们喜欢做的，用我的说法，就是在篮筐附近晃悠。我们不去跨越三英尺高的栏，我们喜欢六英寸高的栏。所以我会定期跑筛选，寻找这些特征。我找的是那种历史上就是超级自由现金流生成器的公司。它们有营收增长在里面，而由于某种原因，它们的企业价值对自由现金流（enterprise value to free cash flow）倍数卖得很低。就好像，Salesforce 怎么跑进来了？这些很棒的公司怎么突然就掉到我们怀里了？我不是篮球运动员，但我懂一些门道。我不投三分球。我就等着那个轻松的反篮。嘿，这儿有只小公司正好掉到我手里，而且没有别人去拦它。我可以跳起来轻松上篮。这就是我们在找的东西。跑筛选，寻找我们关键的基本面指标。我基本上从不看卖方研究（street research）。大多数评论我也不看。我就守着我们自己的数字作为起点。好的。

turns.en: I'm not a basketball player either, but I do appreciate the analogy and I do watch my Celtics. So, you know, I always love to hear things like that.
turns.zh: 我也不是篮球运动员，但我确实很欣赏这个比喻，我也确实看我的 Celtics（凯尔特人队）比赛。所以，你知道，我总是喜欢听到这类说法。

turns.en: Okay.
turns.zh: 好的。

turns.en: So if you, once you have your screens, can you kind of take us from that process of when a company first gets on your radar and You know, what happens between that moment and then when it actually enters, you know, between that and then if it actually enters the portfolio.
turns.zh: 那么，一旦你跑完筛选，你能不能带我们走一遍这个流程——从一家公司第一次进入你的雷达视野，到那之后发生了什么，一直到它真正进入投资组合（如果它真的进入的话）之间。

turns.en: Right. This is the part that can take a lot of time. And what I try to avoid doing is kind of a sunk cost risk. So what I do is I go through our checklist. Everyone's got a checklist. It's pretty extensive. And as soon as something fails the checklist, I drop it. I try to drop it as soon as possible. So the declining order of the checklist is things that, are most relevant that we think, you know, talk about the prospects of the company. We've already talked about a number of the fundamental multiples, you know, the screening kind of things. I like bigger market caps. Again, it gives us a little bit more liquidity that we need. And, you know, we like to look at sales growth over the past five years, of course, P's. I like to see what forward P's are. They're always kind of fun. I don't know how accurate they are. You know, nowadays, of course, like everybody, I just... Go to AI, you know, and you can go to various AI things and just type in something like scrutinize the company's regulatory filings and market information to come up with a detailed financial analysis. Boom. Take a look at it and see if there's something interesting that I haven't. That'd be probably the second or third layer down. And then I go through, you know, the usual, you know, ratios and valuations. I'd like to see returns on assets. And then I'll start going through the 10Ks, looking for impairment if they are an acquirer. if they have made a lot of acquisitions and then start taking impairments, that's a huge red flag for us. And there are a number of other ones, but basically it's just kind of going through a checklist with declining order of importance. Okay.
turns.zh: 对。这一部分可能会花很多时间。我尽量避免的是一种沉没成本风险（sunk cost risk）。所以我的做法是过一遍我们的清单（checklist）。每个人都有一份清单。我们的相当详尽。一旦某样东西通不过清单，我就把它剔除。我会尽量尽早剔除。清单是按重要性递减排列的，排在前面的就是我们觉得最相关、最能反映公司前景的那些东西。我们已经谈过一些基本面倍数了，也就是筛选那类的东西。我喜欢更大的市值。同样，这能给我们多一点所需的流动性。而且，你知道，我们喜欢看过去五年的销售增长，当然还有市盈率（P/E）。我喜欢看前瞻市盈率（forward P/E）是多少。它们总是挺有意思的。我不知道它们有多准确。你知道，现在嘛，跟大家一样，我就……直接去问 AI，你可以用各种 AI 工具，输入类似“仔细审查公司的监管文件和市场信息，给出一份详尽的财务分析”这样的话。搞定。看一眼，看看有没有什么我没注意到的有趣之处。这大概会排在第二或第三层。然后我会过一遍那些常规的比率和估值。我想看资产回报率。接着我会开始翻 10-K 年报，如果它是一家收购方，就找减值（impairment）。如果他们做了大量收购、然后开始计提减值，那对我们来说是个巨大的危险信号。还有其他一些项，但基本上就是按重要性递减的顺序过一遍清单而已。好的。

turns.en: Do you think there's anything in your research that you emphasize you think that other investors might underweight or miss altogether?
turns.zh: 你觉得在你的研究里，有没有什么是你特别强调、而你认为其他投资者可能会低估、甚至完全忽略的？

turns.en: Well, I think one of the things that we underweight is the narrative. And there's so much discussion about this, that, and the other thing. I find that that can be distracting. So I'm amazed that people just simply don't look at what has been the history of this company to generate free cash flow. And once they get that free cash flow, how do they employ that? So I'd say what we underweight substantially is the narrative. For instance, you know, the saspocalypse narrative was a great opportunity for us to pick up some really wonderful companies. It's amusing to us that, you know, that at one point people are saying, oh, well, you know, Chet, GBT is not going to make it, and now it's a darling. Anthropic's not going to make it, and now it's a darling. These goes back and forth. You know, one of the interesting things, of course, for those mathematically inclined is that in a regression analysis, the more variables you include, the more likely you're going to get an index like return. So we tried to focus on a few key variables that will end up with the kind of returns we're looking for. So our focus is a lot less broad than most. Okay.
turns.zh: 嗯，我觉得我们低估的东西之一就是叙事（narrative）。关于这个、那个和其他各种事情的讨论实在太多了。我发现那会让人分心。所以我很惊讶，人们居然不去看这家公司一直以来创造自由现金流的历史，以及一旦他们拿到了这些自由现金流，又是怎么加以运用的。所以我会说，我们大幅低估的就是叙事。比如说，你知道，那场“SaaS 末日”（SaaSpocalypse）叙事对我们来说是个绝佳的机会，让我们捡到了一些真正很棒的公司。让我们觉得好笑的是，一度人们还在说，哦，ChatGPT 撑不下去了，而现在它成了宠儿；Anthropic 撑不下去了，而现在它也成了宠儿。这些说法来回摇摆。当然，对偏爱数学的人来说，有件有意思的事是：在回归分析里，你纳入的变量越多，你就越可能得到一种类似指数的回报。所以我们尽量聚焦于少数几个关键变量，最终得到我们所追求的那种回报。因此我们的关注面比大多数人都要窄得多。好的。

turns.en: The other thing I did want to ask you is, you know, it's a pretty concentrated portfolio. I think when I was looking at the holdings, I think your three largest positions are about two thirds of the fund. What does a company have to do to demonstrate, you know, that, that makes you that comfortable to have these large positions?
turns.zh: 我还想问你的一件事是，你知道，这是一个相当集中的投资组合。我记得我在看持仓的时候，你前三大持仓大概占了基金的三分之二。一家公司得做到什么、证明什么，才能让你如此放心地持有这么大的仓位？

turns.en: You know, I just don't think they can. You know, our view is that buying a new company is kind of like a blind date, if you will. So our typical entry position is around 3% to 4%, and we just like to watch it grow. Our philosophy is let the winners ride. You know, the position that Alphabet has taken in our portfolio is because it's been a fantastic grower Huge capital appreciation. You know, MasterCard, it's kind of just, just to brag for a second, you know, MasterCard, our cost for the stock, which is what now it's selling around $ 580, is around $ 9 a share. When we bought that, it was probably a 3% position, and now it's just grown amazingly.
turns.zh: 你知道，我根本不觉得它们能一开始就证明。我们的观点是，买一家新公司有点像相亲（blind date）。所以我们典型的建仓仓位大概在 3% 到 4%，然后我们就喜欢看着它成长。我们的理念是让赢家继续跑（let the winners ride）。你看，Alphabet 在我们投资组合里能占到那么大的仓位，就是因为它一直是一个出色的成长者，资本增值巨大。再说 MasterCard，容我自夸一下，MasterCard 现在股价大约在 580 美元，而我们的持仓成本大约是每股 9 美元。我们买它的时候，它大概是个 3% 的仓位，而现在它已经惊人地成长起来了。

turns.en: So on the other side of that, you know, when you have these large positions, is there anything you do to, you know, just challenge your thesis to see if they should stay there?
turns.zh: 那么从另一面来说，当你持有这些大仓位时，你会不会做些什么来挑战自己的投资逻辑，看看它们是否应该继续留在那里？

turns.en: Constantly. I'm terrified that our companies are going to let us down. It's like they're going to ghost us suddenly with their capital returns. Like Google. I mean, Alphabet, excuse me. Now, for the first time in history, it has negative free cash flow. I said, how can you do that to me? I've been a loyal investor. And that is a terrible thing to see. I am giving them and management the benefit of the doubt that they're going to go back to their 30% returns on capital employed when we get through this AI cycle. They know AI better than I do. I have a feeling that folk at Alphabet have, you know, they know everything about AI that I'll never learn. And so I'm trusting that they, with their established track record, will do it again and get those returns on capital employed that we're looking for. Okay.
turns.zh: 一直在做。我很害怕我们的公司会让我们失望。就好像它们会突然在资本回报上“人间蒸发”（ghost us）一样。比如 Google，我是说 Alphabet，抱歉。现在，它历史上第一次出现了负的自由现金流。我说，你怎么能这么对我？我可一直是个忠实的投资者。看到这种情况真糟糕。我愿意给他们、给管理层一个善意的推定：等我们熬过这轮 AI 周期，他们会重新回到 30% 的已动用资本回报率。他们比我更懂 AI。我有一种感觉，Alphabet 那帮人，你知道，他们了解关于 AI 的一切，而那些是我永远学不会的。所以我信任他们，凭着他们已经建立的业绩记录，会再次做到，拿到我们所追求的那些已动用资本回报率。好的。

turns.en: And you kind of alluded to this earlier, you know, I want to kind of dive into your sell discipline. You know, you mentioned kind of replacing an investment when another opportunity arises with better potential. How do you make those comparisons when you're looking at businesses that are in different industries?
turns.zh: 你刚才也提到了这一点，我想深入谈谈你的卖出纪律（sell discipline）。你提到当另一个更具潜力的机会出现时，会用它来替换掉一项投资。当你在比较处于不同行业的企业时，你是怎么做这种比较的？

turns.en: A sell is never a pleasant thing. It's a divorce for us. I mean, our portfolio turnover, as you've seen probably in the last five years, is average around 5%. There's some things, however, we won't tolerate, and that is we won't tolerate an operating loss, no matter what happens. A company that reports an operating loss is just gone next day, period. Declining revenue is a big red flag. That means customers are leaving. You don't like that. And of course, negative free cash flow, giving some special companies the benefit of the doubt. And no matter how exciting the story, we avoid companies making large acquisitions. That means what they're saying is the large acquisitions say more than 25% of their market cap. That means the 75% of the combined company has a lousy business. We should have known that. And then if they're making frequent changes of top management, that means maybe the top management isn't that good. Or announcing a novel corporate strategy. I just don't want to hear about it because that's the future. Let them prove them. It's a show me story at that case. So to reinvest, what we're looking for are the famous pools of profitability. So in the airplane business, let's not invest in a public carrier like United Airlines. Great company, I'm sure. Let's invest in the company that supplies them parts like a hiker or something like that. That's where the pools of profitability are. The challenge is this kind of redeployment or this reinvestment challenge, but also the tax implications to our investors. So we're trying to be very careful on saddling them with taxes. So that's another challenge for us. That makes sense.
turns.zh: 卖出从来不是一件愉快的事。对我们来说，那就像是一场离婚。我是说，我们的投资组合换手率，你在过去五年里大概也看到了，平均在 5% 左右。不过，有些事情我们是不会容忍的，那就是我们绝不容忍经营亏损（operating loss），无论发生什么。一家报出经营亏损的公司，第二天就直接清掉，没有例外。营收下滑是个大危险信号。那意味着客户在流失。你不会喜欢那样。当然，还有负的自由现金流——尽管我们会给某些特别的公司一点善意推定。而且无论故事多么激动人心，我们都会避开进行大额收购的公司。大额收购的意思是——收购规模超过它们市值的 25%。这就意味着合并后公司的 75% 是一门糟糕的生意。这一点我们本该早就看出来。然后，如果他们频繁更换高层管理者，那可能意味着高层管理并不那么出色。或者宣布一套全新的公司战略。我就是不想听那一套，因为那都是关于未来的。让他们证明给自己看吧。那种情况下，这就是一个“拿成绩说话”（show me）的故事。那么谈到再投资，我们寻找的是那些著名的“盈利池”（pools of profitability）。所以在飞机这个行业里，我们不去投资像 United Airlines 这样的公共航空公司。我相信它是家很棒的公司。我们去投资给他们供应零件的公司，比如 Haiker 之类的。那才是盈利池所在的地方。挑战就在于这种资金重新配置、或者说再投资的难题，但同时还有对投资者的税务影响。所以我们尽量非常小心，不让他们背上税务负担。这对我们来说又是一个挑战。这说得通。

turns.en: If one of your holdings is seeing selling pressure in the market, how do you determine whether it's giving you an opportunity to add to your position or kind of signaling, you know, maybe you need to take another look at your thesis?
turns.zh: 如果你持有的某只股票在市场上正遭遇抛售压力，你是如何判断这究竟是给了你一个加仓的机会，还是在暗示——你知道——也许你需要重新审视一下自己的投资逻辑？

turns.en: Yeah. Well, I mean, obviously we're not perfect. The market, you know, everyone says, well, everyone's a contrarian nowadays. And I think the stats that you hear are that, you know, basically 80% of the time, the people that are selling are right. But that's a 20% position that we're looking for. So we test it. If we buy something and it immediately goes down, which seems to often be the case right away, that's kind of shame on us. We do try to look for relative strength and we're making it, you know, we'll eye a company and we'll say, gosh, this is a great company. It's still going down. Maybe there's a large seller out there, you know, Fidelity or Vanguard or BlackRock is rebalancing or something. Let's not get in the way of the steamroller. But if it picks up again, we'll kind of get in there. We look for, so relative strength is nice. calendar quarter of all these fundamentals improving on the business so um but sometimes the opportunity is just there and you need to jump on it when you have total conviction that's we talked earlier david about the you know margin for error and this is a classic case you know is this is it so cheap that you have a great margin for error or is it just like a great company that's maybe you know market price so let's let's give it a couple uh more quarters to see what happens.
turns.zh: 是啊。嗯，我是说，显然我们并不完美。市场嘛，你知道，现在人人都说自己是逆向投资者（contrarian）。而我觉得你会听到的统计数据是，基本上有 80% 的时候，卖出的人是对的。但我们要找的正是那 20% 的情形。所以我们会去检验它。如果我们买入某样东西，它立刻就跌了——而这似乎常常是一买就发生的事——那就算是我们的失误。我们确实会设法寻找相对强度（relative strength），在我们下手的时候，我们会盯上一家公司，然后说，天呐，这真是家很棒的公司。可它还在跌。也许外面有个大卖家，你知道，Fidelity、Vanguard 或者 BlackRock 在做再平衡之类的。那我们可别去挡压路机的道。但如果它重新涨起来，我们就会进场。我们寻找的是——所以相对强度是件好事。一个日历季度里，这家公司所有的基本面都在改善，所以……嗯，但有时候机会就摆在那儿，当你有十足的信念时，你就得抓住它。这就是我们之前谈到的，David，关于安全边际的问题，而这正是个经典案例：它是不是便宜到你拥有很好的安全边际，还是说它只是一家很棒的公司、股价大概就在合理水平，那就让我们再多观察几个季度，看看会发生什么。

turns.en: Okay. And, you know, we talked a little bit about Alphabet and you did mention MasterCard and, you know, the other company I think I saw that was Lamb Research and, you know, these are all different businesses, you know, very, very different, you know, aside from, you know, some of the things you were looking in terms of cash flows, are there other common characteristics you see in the three of them that would explain why they're all such significant pieces or are they all kind of just winners in terms of market appreciation?
turns.zh: 好的。我们刚才稍微谈到了 Alphabet，你也提到了 MasterCard，还有我记得看到的另一家公司是 Lamb Research（Lam Research）。这些都是不同的企业，非常非常不同。除了你在现金流方面看重的那些东西之外，你在这三家公司身上还看到有哪些共同的特征，能够解释为什么它们都是如此重要的持仓？还是说它们只是从市场升值的角度来看都算是赢家？

turns.en: They're all winners, certainly for market appreciation. But I'd say the thing they, you know, I was looking over some stats for them recently, and I thought, you know, what they do have in common, but not unusual, I'm happy to say, in our portfolio, is return on capital employed. So here we've got MasterCard, with a 66% return on capital. That is unbelievable. I mean, that's an incredible business. And then you've got Google has kind of come down recently at a 28% level. This is like five-year average. And then Lamb is a 52% return on capital. They have just got a great business where they can reinvest and just keep those earnings going. And that is so important for the compounding effect that we're looking for. And, you know, frankly, I know this is kind of making a point here, but I would invest in a buggy whip company if it could demonstrate 66% returns on capital employed. I mean, someone's out there definitely ordering buggy whips. I don't have to know about that. This is a great management team. Look at those whips. They're fabulous. And the free cash flow just pours in, and that's neat. Okay.
turns.zh: 它们都是赢家，从市场升值来看当然是这样。但我会说，我最近在看它们的一些数据，我就想，它们确实有的一个共同点——不过我很高兴地说，这在我们投资组合里并不罕见——就是已动用资本回报率。你看，我们这儿的 MasterCard，资本回报率高达 66%。这简直难以置信。我是说，那是一门不可思议的生意。然后 Google 最近有点回落，在 28% 的水平。这大概是五年平均值。再看 Lamb，资本回报率是 52%。它们就是拥有很棒的生意，能够不断再投资、让盈利持续下去。这对我们所追求的复利效应太重要了。而且，坦白说，我知道这有点像是在举个例子，但如果一家做马鞭（buggy whip）的公司能证明自己有 66% 的已动用资本回报率，我也会投资它。我是说，外面肯定有人在订购马鞭。我不需要了解那些。这是一支出色的管理团队。看看那些鞭子，棒极了。自由现金流就这么滚滚而来，那真是不错。好的。

turns.en: You know, I did want to ask about, you know, just the market we're in, you know, obviously, as I track funds and the market and things like that, you know, there seems to be a small group of large companies really have commanded a lot of attention, you know, whether it's investors or the media, especially around AI. You know, as a stock picker, how do you determine where there's durable economics behind this, you know, shall we say AI enthusiasm and, you know, where expectations may simply run too far?
turns.zh: 你知道，我确实想问问我们所处的这个市场。显然，因为我跟踪基金和市场等等，似乎有一小撮大公司真的吸引了大量关注，无论是投资者还是媒体，尤其是围绕 AI 这块。那么作为一名选股者，你是如何判断在这股——我们姑且称之为 AI 热情——的背后，哪里存在持久的经济效益（durable economics），而哪里的预期又可能单纯是跑得太远了？

turns.en: I tried to look at some of these financials and they're a little bit of a head shaker. It's too early for us. There are people who have much more information or know more or are willing to put it all in red that are moving the markets around in this area. This is a narrative question that I am not capable of figuring out. A lot of people think they are capable of figuring out. We were not the original investor in MasterCard and we were not the original investor in Alphabet. As a matter of fact, I think we established the bulk of our Alphabet position during COVID when it was unbelievable. We sold down to, I don't know, it was like 16 times earnings. So we're not an early person, but I'd like to see the track record of all these businesses five years from now and see who's generating the free cash flow that we like. Okay.
turns.zh: 我试着去看这些公司的一些财务数据，它们有点让人摸不着头脑。对我们来说还太早了。在这个领域里，有一些人掌握着多得多的信息、懂得更多，或者愿意把一切都押上去，正是他们在搅动这个板块的市场。这是一个叙事层面的问题，而我没有能力把它搞清楚。很多人却自以为有能力搞清楚。我们并不是 MasterCard 最早的那批投资者，也不是 Alphabet 最早的那批投资者。事实上，我想我们大部分 Alphabet 的仓位是在新冠疫情期间建立的，那时候它便宜得难以置信。它一度跌到，我不知道，大概是 16 倍市盈率。所以我们不是那种抢先下手的人，但我想看看五年之后所有这些企业的业绩记录，看看谁在创造我们所喜欢的那种自由现金流。好的。

turns.en: And also, you've been investing for a while, and so it's been through different interest rate inflation regimes. In today's environment, do you think the hurdle rate you require from equity has changed?
turns.zh: 还有，你已经投资很长一段时间了，所以经历过不同的利率和通胀环境。在今天的环境下，你觉得你对股票所要求的门槛回报率（hurdle rate）有没有发生变化？

turns.en: You know, our funds can use leverage. And leverage, of course, can be super dangerous in sharply declining markets and so on and so forth. So we're very careful about it. You know, a real kind of simple rule of thumb is, When interest rates are stable and we're lower, we just compare free cash flow yields to our cost of borrowing. And you can kind of almost arbitrage the businesses that you own and what it costs you to own them. It's kind of neat. These days, now that the, you know, 30 years, well over 5%, 5.3, and then we've got the 10 year at the 4.7, it's scary. Highly indebted companies have problems. I've never liked highly indebted companies that much. And now I try to avoid them as much as I possibly can.
turns.zh: 你知道，我们的基金可以使用杠杆。而杠杆，当然，在市场急剧下跌等情况下可能极其危险。所以我们对此非常谨慎。有一个非常简单的经验法则是：当利率稳定且处于较低水平时，我们就把自由现金流收益率和我们的借贷成本做比较。这样你几乎可以在你所拥有的企业和持有它们的成本之间做套利。这挺巧妙的。而这些天，如今 30 年期国债收益率已经超过 5%，到了 5.3%，10 年期在 4.7%，这就吓人了。高负债的公司会有麻烦。我从来就不怎么喜欢高负债的公司。而现在我尽量尽可能地避开它们。

turns.en: So were there businesses that looked attractive or more attractive when capital was nearly free that just don't work anymore?
turns.zh: 那么，有没有哪些企业，在资本几乎免费的时候看起来很有吸引力、或者更有吸引力，但现在就完全行不通了？

turns.en: Oh, yeah. I mean, when capitals are really free, the growth side of the market just became absurdly priced. They were valued for that dotted line that goes up to infinity. And value was unbelievably cheap. One of the funny things is that we follow our nose for yields, free cash flow yields, et cetera. And we're putting our toe into a bunch of companies I wouldn't have touched before that have gotten so cheap as growth has become discounted with higher rates. So it's kind of a, I hate to say contrarian, but it's just kind of this way of getting into the cheaper side of the market if you look for these fundamental yields and we don't You know, we don't have to, as you pointed out at the very beginning of our discussion, have to worry about whether our style is growth or value. Our style is capital appreciation.
turns.zh: 哦，是啊。我是说，当资本真的很便宜的时候，市场的成长那一端价格就变得荒唐。它们的估值是按那条一路冲向无穷的虚线来给的。而价值股则便宜得难以置信。有意思的一点是，我们跟着收益率走——自由现金流收益率等等。我们正在试探性地买入一堆我以前根本不会碰的公司，因为随着利率上升、成长被折价，这些公司已经变得如此便宜。所以这有点——我不太愿意说是逆向投资——但这就是如果你去寻找这些基本面收益率，就能进入市场更便宜那一端的一种方式。而且，正如你在我们讨论一开始就指出的，我们不必担心自己的风格是成长还是价值。我们的风格是资本增值（capital appreciation）。

turns.en: Okay. And I just got one more question before we, this is probably more of a broad picture, but, you know, since you've been managing money for a couple decades, what's something you believe about investing today that you didn't believe 20 years ago?
turns.zh: 好的。在我们结束之前我还有最后一个问题，这大概更偏向宏观层面，但你知道，既然你已经管理资金好几十年了，有没有什么是你今天相信、但 20 年前并不相信的关于投资的道理？

turns.en: 20 years ago is a long time to remember anything, by the way, when you get to my age. This is a test. I should have written all this stuff down 20 years ago. But I would say that knowing the numbers is everything. And if you know the numbers, you've got confidence that in what you own and you can hold it when markets go down or buy when narratives drive the stocks down. I find that narratives are what give you the opportunities and test your resolve. You know, it's a well-known stat, I guess. I It's very important to me that stock markets on average tend to go down about 15% in any calendar year. And sometimes it's much more, 30% in some years. But on average, the market goes down. And everyone talks about, oh, are we in a bull? Is this technically a bear market? Or is this not a bear market? I don't know. 15% is a stomach. A lot of people just run, as I like to say, throw down their musket and run when it goes down 15%. It's the end of the world. But So I don't think investing takes guts, which is what I thought about maybe 20 years ago. Investing just takes the, the knowledge of your numbers and what you own and know what you're doing. And then you can eliminate all that risk and you don't need guts. If you have knowledge, you don't need guts. You can just be as wimpy as I am and do pretty well.
turns.zh: 顺便说一句，到了我这个年纪，20 年前的事要记起来可是很长的一段时间。这是道考验题。我 20 年前就该把这些东西都写下来。但我会说，懂那些数字就是一切。如果你懂这些数字，你对自己所持有的东西就有信心，你就能在市场下跌时拿得住，或者在叙事把股价打下去时买入。我发现，正是叙事给了你机会，也考验你的决心。你知道，这大概是个众所周知的统计数据。对我来说很重要的一点是，股市在任何一个日历年里平均往往会下跌大约 15%。有时候还远不止，有些年份会跌 30%。但平均而言，市场是会下跌的。而人人都在谈，哦，我们是牛市吗？这在技术上算熊市吗？还是不算熊市？我不知道。15% 是能让人受不了的。很多人就是会跑，就像我喜欢说的，一跌 15% 就扔下手里的滑膛枪（musket）夺路而逃。感觉像是世界末日。所以，我并不认为投资需要胆量——而这也许正是我 20 年前的想法。投资只需要你懂那些数字、懂你持有的东西、懂自己在做什么。这样一来，你就能消除掉所有这些风险，也就不需要胆量了。如果你有知识，你就不需要胆量。你可以像我一样胆小，照样做得挺好。

turns.en: Well, I like that. Not the last part, but, uh, you know, but you know what you're saying, um, No, but this was a lot of fun. We need to end here, but this was a great discussion. Tom, thanks again for joining me.
turns.zh: 嗯，我喜欢这个说法。倒不是最后那部分，不过，呃，你知道，我明白你的意思。嗯，不，这真的很有意思。我们得在这里结束了，但这是一场很棒的讨论。Tom，再次感谢你来做客。

turns.en: David, what a pleasure. I look forward to many more of your podcasts.
turns.zh: David，非常荣幸。我期待你更多的播客节目。
